sentences.text: The case of the petitioners is that they have purchased the aforesaid plot by sale deed dated 10.05.2024.

Thereafter, on 24.09.2024 a notification under Section 11 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 was issued notifying the intention of the respondents to acquire the said land along with adjoining lands.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioners have filed objection against the preliminary notification under Section 11 on 29.09.2024.
They apprehend that their objections would not be decided and therefore, the instant petition has been filed.

3. It is noteworthy that except for raising the grievance that the objection filed by the petitioners is not being decided there is no other ground on which the preliminary notification can be struck down.

4. Sri D.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the Development Authority points out that in the preliminary notification itself, sixty days time is provided to any person who is likely to be affected by the notification or aggrieved thereby to file objections.

He submits that in such circumstances,
the apprehension of the petitioners is unfounded.
5. We found sufficient force in the submission.

As the preliminary notification itself permits filing of objections and therefore, we have no reason to doubt that the objections filed by the petitioners would not be considered in accordance with law.
Therefore, the writ petition is disposed of without any further direction.
